name: Grounds Maintenance
summary: Mowing, bed care, pruning and seasonal cleanups on a schedule you agree in writing.

seo.title: Grounds maintenance in Greater Victoria | RNC Landscaping
seo.description: Scheduled mowing, bed care, pruning and seasonal cleanups for homes, stratas and commercial sites in Greater Victoria, with a written visit scope. Free quote.

hero.lede: Mowing, bed care, pruning and seasonal cleanups on a set schedule, planned for wet winters, dry summers and the CRD watering rules. A written scope says what each visit covers.

audiences.title: Homeowners
audiences.body: A tidy lawn and healthy beds without managing it yourself. We agree on what each visit includes and how often we come, then we keep to it.

audiences.title: Strata councils and property managers
audiences.body: A written scope and visit schedule you can take to council, one contact for owner concerns, and a seasonal plan for the whole complex. See [commercial and strata service](/commercial/).

audiences.title: Commercial and institutional sites
audiences.body: Work to your specification, scheduled around tenants, students or patients, with insurance and safety documents on request.

includes.title: Lawn care
includes.body: Mowing, edging and string trimming, plus aeration, overseeding and moss control when the lawn needs it.

includes.title: Bed care
includes.body: Weeding, deadheading, cutting back perennials, edging bed lines and topping up mulch.

includes.title: Pruning
includes.body: Hedges, shrubs and small ornamental trees pruned at the right time of year for each plant. Larger trees go to our [tree and vegetation service](/services/tree-vegetation/).

includes.title: Seasonal cleanups
includes.body: Spring start-up, fall leaf removal and cut-back, and storm debris cleanup after winter wind.

includes.title: Green waste removal
includes.body: We haul clippings and debris away. Invasive plants are bagged and disposed of to CRD rules.

includes.title: Visit notes
includes.body: On recurring work we note anything we see that needs attention, such as a broken sprinkler head or a leaning tree, and tell you before we act.

goodFitIf.heading: Good fit if…
items: You want the yard kept to one standard without managing it yourself
Your strata council needs a written scope and visit calendar it can approve
You manage several sites and want visit notes and issue reports in writing
You are away for part of the year and want someone checking the property
Your current contractor's visits are hard to plan around tenants or residents
Mowing at a taller height in dry spells
Checking irrigation suits CRD lawn days
Drains cleared of leaves where included

process.title: Tell us about the property
process.body: Use the [free quote form](/free-quote/) to share the municipality, property type and what you need.
process.deliverable: Your request, sent from your own email app

process.title: Site walk
process.body: We walk the property with you or your site contact and note lawn areas, beds, hedges and access.
process.deliverable: A list of questions answered on the spot

process.title: Written scope and schedule
process.body: You get a written quote that lists the tasks per visit, the visit frequency and the season it covers.
process.deliverable: A written scope and visit calendar

process.title: Regular visits
process.body: The crew works to the scope. Questions and changes go through one contact.

process.title: Seasonal check-in
process.body: Before each season we review what is working and adjust the plan with you.
process.deliverable: An updated plan for the next season

localRules.heading: Local rules that affect maintenance
localRules.intro: Two regional rules shape routine grounds care across Greater Victoria. Municipal tree bylaws also apply to hedges and larger pruning; see your [area page](/areas/).

items.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply. Lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm. Hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day.

The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program asks for invasive plants to be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

localRules.areasLink: See the rules for your municipality on our [service area pages](/areas/).

faqs.a: It depends on the property and the season. Many lawns need weekly or every-other-week visits in spring and early summer and fewer in winter. Your quote states the visit frequency.
Yes. Greater Victoria's mild winters mean pruning, cleanups and storm debris work continue through the cooler months.

faqs.q: Can you quote to our existing strata specification?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the specification with your quote request and we will quote to it and list any questions.

faqs.q: What happens to the green waste?
faqs.a: We remove it. Invasive plants are kept separate and disposed of following CRD guidance.

faqs.q: Will you tell us about problems you notice?
faqs.a: Yes. On recurring work we note things like a broken sprinkler head or a leaning tree and tell you before we act, so nothing outside the scope happens without your say.

faqs.q: Do I need to be home for visits?
faqs.a: No, as long as the crew can reach the work area safely. Tell us about gates, pets and parking when you request a quote.
